prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer–loading handoff; airline loading excluded; no explicit modes. Baggage Control System (Velvet) links bag/passenger/flight records, validates identity/routing/current schedules, applies approved screening profiles/time-effective sort plans; alternates require valid screening/timing. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) maintains flight identifiers/destinations/departures/revisions/airline dispatch targets/connection windows; timestamps changes; supplies routing records/sends Flight Cutoff Advisory (recipient unspecified). Dispatch time prioritizes; departure time is passenger-facing. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates readiness/restrictions/availability; produces Recovery Route Card. Congestion uses lane availability/stops/incoming rate. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) sets thresholds/overload responses; coordinates staffing/readiness/recovery with Security Duty Manager/Maintenance Technician; authorizes plan recovery after cause correction; escalations notify Security Duty Manager. Maintenance Technician isolates failures/confirms safe restart. Staff verify eligibility/identity/flight/size/weight; resolve data before induction. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance/sends Oversize Exception Ticket; oversize requires designated holding/staff-approved routing. Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable tags/Calibration Witness Tag. Transfer Bag Feeder records arrivals/sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds until screening/onward handling confirmed. Induction Tray Conveyor spaces bags; jams/open doors/downstream unreadiness interlock. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner identify/image/report dispositions; latter produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Incomplete examinations/mismatches prohibit clearance/identity-dependent routing. Image Resolution Desk reviews images/identity/prompts, records dispositions/resolves image holds before return; pending review bars make-up. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity/screening/destination; sends Chute Occupancy Note; blocked/unavailable chutes prohibit release. Bag Reconciliation Station compares active records/flags discrepancies/sends Bag Match Query. Alarm/unresolved/destination/handling-limit exceptions divert to Secondary Inspection Chute; duty-authorized access. Inspection staff retain alarms; isolation secures area/notifies supervisor. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) manages security holds/coordinates airport security personnel. Return requires identity/examination/authorization agreement; stopped/misdirected bags await location/identity. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor follow plan/capacity. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages screened/authorized bags within flight window/reports constrained

New part:
S109: Baggage Control System applies cutoff profiles configured for each carrier, flight, and operating condition.
S110: A bag accepted before cutoff retains its assigned flight unless a subsequent schedule or operational change requires reassessment.
S111: When schedule revisions move a departure earlier, Baggage Operations Supervisor reviews affected flights and directs priority adjustments.
S112: Cutoff values account for screening, sortation, make-up, and transfer handling allowances rather than only aircraft departure.
S113: Baggage Control System receives the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
S114: Baggage Control System compares remaining processing time with route-specific handling estimates.
S115: Bags with confirmed screening clearance may proceed to flight-specific sort destinations when capacity is available.
S116: Bags awaiting screening are held from final flight induction even when their scheduled departure is near.
S117: North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner record screening outcomes for inducted bags.
S118: The Image Resolution Desk reviews unresolved images, and final routing remains withheld until disposition is recorded.
S119: A positive threat indication suspends ordinary routing until the authorized security disposition is entered.
S120: Explosives Response Team produces the Custody Seal Log.
S121: When screening disposition is pending, Baggage Control System preserves a recoverable bag-to-flight association rather than releasing the bag to make-up.
S122: Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes eligible bags according to flight assignment and current cutoff priority.
S123: Concourse Zone Controller coordinates induction demand with available conveyor capacity across the operating area.
S124: Induction Tray Conveyor admits bags in priority order, subject to scan confirmation and safe spacing.
S125: East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor receive flight groups according to active allocation rules.
S126: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit presents bags for outbound loading only after flight grouping and screening status are confirmed.
S127: Outbound Load Control Desk uses planned dispatch time and load-close targets to monitor whether assigned bags can be accepted.
S128: Airline Ramp Coordinator reports changes to loading readiness that could alter the usable cutoff.
S129: Baggage Operations Supervisor may defer lower-priority bags when a flight's remaining processing window is insufficient.
S130: Bags missing the active flight cutoff are held for reassignment or recovery rather than routed into an unavailable departure build.
S131: Make-up allocation begins when the active flight assignment and available build positions are confirmed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
